title: a / an / some / any / much / many
grammarTitle: a / an / some / any / much / many / a few / a little
grammarNote: Эти слова называются КВАНТОРАМИ — они говорят нам, СКОЛЬКО чего-то. Выбор зависит от двух вещей: 1) существительное исчисляемое или нет; 2) предложение утвердительное, отрицательное или вопросительное. Правильный выбор квантора — одна из самых важных грамматических тем в английском!

grammarTable.subject: a / an
grammarTable.example: a tomato · an apple · a café · Have an egg for breakfast.

grammarTable.subject: some
grammarTable.example: some apples · some water · some bread · I'd like some tea.

grammarTable.subject: any
grammarTable.example: Is there any milk? · I don't have any eggs. · Any bread left?

grammarTable.subject: much
grammarTable.example: How much sugar? · Not much water. · Is there much time?

grammarTable.subject: many
grammarTable.example: How many eggs? · Not many cafés. · Are there many students?

grammarTable.subject: a lot of
grammarTable.example: a lot of apples · a lot of milk · There's a lot of food here.

grammarTable.example: a few tomatoes · a few minutes · I have a few ideas.

grammarTable.subject: a little
grammarTable.example: a little sugar · a little water · just a little honey.

grammarExtra.title: some vs any — the key rule

rows.example: There is some milk in the fridge. ✅ · I want some tea. ✅
Is there any milk? ✅ · Do you have any eggs? ✅
There isn't any milk. ✅ · I don't have any bread. ✅
Would you like some tea? ✅ · Can I have some water? ✅
You can have any cake you want. ✅ · Come any time. ✅
❌ Usually wrong in questions. → Is there any milk? ✅

grammarExtra.title: much vs many — and a lot of

rows.example: How much sugar? · Not much time. · There's too much salt!
How many eggs? · Not many people. · Too many dishes!
a lot of sugar ✅ · a lot of eggs ✅ · a lot of time ✅
"There are lots of options on the menu!" (spoken)
"There is much food" (formal) → prefer "a lot of food".

rows.form: too much / too many = negative excess
rows.example: "There's too much salt!" · "Too many people in here!"

grammarExtra.title: a few vs a little (positive meaning)

rows.example: I have a few tomatoes — enough for a salad.
Just add a little salt — not too much.
There are few options — I'm not happy.
There's little water left — we need more.
a few friends came ✅ (positive) vs few friends (sad, almost none)
a little time left ✅ (positive) vs little time (worrying)
✅ I don't have any milk. (negatives use "any"!)
✅ Is there any cheese? (questions usually use "any"!)
✅ How much rice? (rice is uncountable!)

rows.form: ❌ I have few ideas for this.
rows.example: ✅ I have a few ideas. ("few" without "a" = almost none — negative!)

grammarTip:
Шпаргалка:
(+) Утверждение: some milk · some apples · a lot of food · a few eggs · a little sugar
(?) Вопрос:       any milk? · any apples? · how much? · how many? · a few? · a little?
(−) Отрицание:   not any milk · not many eggs · not much sugar · no bread at all

💡 ИСКЛЮЧЕНИЕ: some в вопросах-предложениях/просьбах:
'Would you like some tea?' ✅  (это предложение, а не вопрос о наличии)
'Can I have some water?' ✅  (это вежливая просьба)

💡 a few vs a little:
a few EGGS (исчисляемое) · a little SUGAR (неисчисляемое)

exercises.text: Is there ___ honey in the jar?
I'd like ___ milk in my tea, please.
exercises.hint: Positive statement → some. "I'd like some milk." ✅

exercises.text: How ___ eggs do we need for the omelette?

exercises.instruction: Choose: a few or a little?
exercises.text: She added ___ sugar to the tea — just enough.

exercises.instruction: Choose: a few or a little?
exercises.text: I have ___ friends coming for dinner — about three.
"I don't have some bread" is correct.
exercises.hint: Negatives use "any": "I don't have any bread." ✅

exercises.text: There is ___ food at the market — it's amazing!
exercises.hint: a lot of + uncountable/countable in positive statements. ✅

exercises.text: "___ rice is left?" — asking about quantity.

exercises.hint: Offers and polite requests → "some", not "any". "Would you like some tea?" ✅

exercises.text: I don't have ___ apples at home — the fridge is empty.
exercises.hint: Negative + countable noun → "any": I don't have any apples.

exercises.text: There are ___ cafés near WKU — only Stepnoy Corner.

questions.text: "___ milk is in the fridge?" — asking about quantity.
I don't have ___ eggs — I need to go to the market.
questions.hint: Negatives → "any": I don't have any eggs.
Offers use "some": Would you like some soup? ✅

questions.text: "There's ___ food at the market — incredible variety!"
questions.hint: "a lot of" = large amount, positive, used with countable and uncountable.

questions.text: "She added just ___ honey — it was perfect."
How ___ apples do we need for the cake?
"Is there some cheese in the fridge?" is correct.
questions.hint: Questions → "any": Is there any cheese? (Some in questions = usually wrong.)

questions.text: "I have ___ ideas — let me share them."
questions.hint: Ideas = countable → "a few ideas" (= some, positive).

questions.text: What is the difference: "a few" vs "few"?
questions.hint: "a few friends" = I have some friends ✅. "few friends" = I have almost none 😞.

questions.text: There are ___ options here — just one or two.
"Too ___ people in the café — let's go elsewhere."
"I only have ___ time — let's be quick."
questions.hint: Time = uncountable → a little time (= some, but not much).

questions.text: Which quantifier works with BOTH countable AND uncountable?
questions.hint: "a lot of" works with both: a lot of apples ✅ · a lot of milk ✅.
